name: Pimsleur
tagline: Organize user-owned audio lessons with spaced recall prompts and progress

tiers.name: Audio-Only, single language
tiers.limits: All available audio lessons for 1 language; course depth varies by language

tiers.name: Premium, single language
tiers.limits: All available levels for 1 language plus reading, Voice Coach, flashcards, and review features

tiers.name: All Access, monthly
tiers.limits: All available levels across 51 languages; all app features

tiers.name: All Access, annual
tiers.limits: All available levels across 50+ languages; billed $164.95 annually
tiers.notes: Effective monthly rate rounded from the official annual total.

tiers.name: All Access, lifetime
tiers.limits: 50+ languages and all available levels; live page lists $798 one-time and a $478.80 promotional checkout price
tiers.notes: One-time purchase, not a subscription; promotional eligibility and expiry can change.

tiers.name: Single-language lifetime
tiers.limits: Permanent access to the selected language/levels; price varies by language and number of levels
tiers.notes: One-time purchase; no single universal price is published.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no permanent free tier (1 sample lesson; paid subscriptions offer a 7-day trial)
pricing.billingTerms: Audio-Only and Premium are monthly; All Access monthly or annual; lifetime products are one-time purchases; trials auto-convert
pricing.hiddenCosts: Course depth varies by language; lifetime discounts are promotional, and app-store prices can differ slightly from direct web prices.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Pimsleur, organize user-owned audio lessons with spaced recall prompts and progress. The hard boundary is licensed audio curriculum, pedagogy, mobile apps, and language catalog, plus content, pedagogy, and network.
coreLoopDIY: Organize user-owned audio lessons into a study plan, schedule spaced retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
requirements: optional speech or language-model API key
whatYouLose: licensed audio curriculum, pedagogy, mobile apps, and language catalog
ongoingBurden: curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Pimsleur because the learning loop is buildable, while trusted curriculum, instructors, feedback, credentials, and community are not. The recurring cost buys curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Moodle
priorArt.desc: Long-running open-source learning platform with courses, assessments, and progress tracking.

alternatives.name: Anki
alternatives.desc: Turns legally owned audio and recall prompts into a scheduled personal course, without supplying Pimsleur's recordings.

facts.install: Use the Windows installer, macOS DMG or official Linux launcher
facts.dataFormat: Local profile files including collection.anki2, collection.media and backups; exports use .apkg/.colpkg, with optional AnkiWeb sync
facts.gapVsPaid: Anki does not include Pimsleur's copyrighted audio course or hands-free conversational pacing; the learner must create every prompt.

alternatives.name: AnkiDroid
alternatives.desc: An offline Android player and scheduler for your own audio recall cards, not a free copy of the copyrighted course.

facts.install: Install from Google Play or F-Droid, or sideload the official APK
facts.dataFormat: An Anki collection and media on the Android device, with .apkg import/export and optional AnkiWeb sync
facts.gapVsPaid: AnkiDroid does not include Pimsleur's audio course or hands-free conversational pacing; the learner must create every recall card.

alternatives.name: Moodle
alternatives.desc: Sequences owned audio lessons, recall activities and progress for a learner or class; setup is much less conversational.

facts.install: Upload the PHP release to a web server, create a database and moodledata directory, then complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Courses, users, grades and settings in SQL; uploaded files in the separate moodledata directory
facts.gapVsPaid: Moodle cannot reproduce Pimsleur's expertly sequenced conversational audio or effortless hands-free lesson flow.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP and database requirements, protected writable storage, cron, SMTP, backups and upgrades are all the operator's responsibility

notes: Editorial comparison targets the All Access plan and a personal study companion DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Pimsleur in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and a service worker for offline use; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize user-owned audio lessons into a study plan, schedule spaced retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Import Markdown, text, or user-authored notes and split them into editable learning units.
Create flashcards and short quizzes only after showing the generated items for approval.
Implement a transparent spaced-repetition schedule with due, again, hard, good, and easy actions.
Add goals, study sessions, streak-free progress charts, notes, and weak-topic review.
For language practice, record the learner and compare timing or pronunciation without presenting medical claims.
Support offline use, full export, reset, backup, and deletion of all learning data.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out licensed premium courses.
Deliberately leave out accredited certificates and grading.
Deliberately leave out live tutors, large classrooms, and a learner marketplace.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
